title: fix(scripts): walk both sides of a pipe in the strict-face measurement twin (objectui#10076)
body:
Fixes #10076

Clause-②: no — a root measurement script that ships nothing; no published contract, accept set or public surface changes

## What changed

`scripts/measure-strict-authoring-face.mjs` (the objectui#7581 MEASUREMENT THROWAWAY) now walks BOTH sides of a zod pipe at every site that walked only `in`. This mirrors the shipped walker behind `deriveStrictAuthoringSchema`.

| site | before | after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `makeTwin` transform (baseline, strict and whole-tree twins) | `in` only | `in` and `out` |
| `makeKeyProbe` probe | `in` only | `in` piped into `out` |
| `unwrapToObject` (the key probe's union and intersection merge) | `in` only | `in`, else `out` |
| `collectNodes` (schema-guided node collection) | `in` only | `in` and `out` |

`unwrapToObject` is a fourth site. It was not on the dispatch's list, but it read `def.in` the same way.

The twin also gains every other arm the shipped walker has and the twin lacked. Each is a one-arm mirror: `set`, `map`, `prefault`, `promise`, and a `default:` arm that reports a schema-bearing wrapper with no arm under `walkerLimits` instead of treating it as a leaf. The key probe and the node collector gain `prefault` and `promise` in their `innerType` group. They get no `set` or `map` arm because they walk JSON values, and a JSON value is never a Set or a Map. The docblock now states the arm list, why the script keeps its own walker, and the one shape where the key probe can now over-report.

⛔ No new gate, no pin file, no edit under `packages/types/**`.

## Why not import the shipped derivation instead (measured)

Each variant below is the script with ONE substitution, run on today's corpora and diffed against the unmodified script's `--json` output. As a control, the harness copy with only its root path pinned reproduces the unmodified output byte-for-byte.

| variant | output vs the unmodified script |
| --- | --- |
| whole-tree twin replaced by `StrictAnyComponentSchema` | identical |
| per-component strict twin replaced by `deriveStrictAuthoringSchema(schema)` | MOVES: nodes strict-refused 168 → 185 across seven component types; strict-clean component types 76 → 72 |
| per-component strict twin replaced by `deriveStrictAuthoringSchema(baselineTwin(schema))` | identical |

The node boundary is load-bearing: without it, a parent node is charged for every child's refusal. The shipped derivation has no boundary, no non-strict mode and no key skeleton. So the `baseline` twin, the key probe and the node collector have no counterpart there. Only the script's own walker can apply the boundary, and that walker needs every traversal arm anyway. Sending only the strict half through the shipped derivation would split the arm table across two files and still leave the script's copy in place. So the arms are mirrored in place instead.

## Evidence, before and after

**Real corpora.** Built with `pnpm --filter @object-ui/types build`, then run with `pnpm exec tsx scripts/measure-strict-authoring-face.mjs --json` and in the markdown form. The output is byte-identical before and after: the `--json` report minus its `pin` block, and the whole markdown report. The last runs were at head `056efaa9b6`, with `corpusMatchesMain: true` against `95a7c8d38f`. On today's face, 163 / 588 documents are refused by the whole-tree strict parse, and 31 / 588 by the tolerant face.

**Synthetic probe.** The script was copied byte-for-byte into a scratch root. That root's `packages/types/dist/zod/index.zod.js` is a shim: it re-exports the real built face and adds one arm:

- `pre: z.preprocess(f, z.object({ a }))`
- `preSlot: z.preprocess(f, z.object({ children: SchemaNodeSchema }))`
- `pref: z.object({ b }).prefault({})`

The scratch corpus holds seven documents: four for that arm and three `filter-builder` documents on the REAL face.

| reading | shipped walker | script before (blob `15f37db94d`) | script after (blob `43f5ba8f99`) |
| --- | --: | --: | --: |
| documents refused, whole-tree strict | 5 / 7 | 0 / 7 | 5 / 7 |
| nodes collected | n/a | 7 | 8 (adds the node under the preprocess slot) |
| nodes strict-refused, per component | n/a | 0 | 5 |
| undeclared keys named by the key probe | n/a | none | `pre.bogusPre`, `pref.bogusPref`, `value.bogusInGroup`, `value.conditions.[].bogusInCondition`, `bogusChild` |

Both controls (a clean synthetic document and a clean `filter-builder` document) stay green in every column. The tolerant face accepts every probe document.

## Premise check: the out side is no longer empty

The card says the two twins agree because "no object currently sits on an `out` side". That was true when the card was filed. It is not true on `95a7c8d38f`. A walk of `AnyComponentSchema` through every schema-bearing member finds three objects on an `out` side:

- `filter-builder` `value`: `FilterBuilderValueSchema` is `z.any().superRefine(…).pipe(FilterGroupSchema)` (objectui#10825, landed 2026-09-27).
- Each `conditions[]` entry of that group: `FilterGroupEntrySchema` pipes into `FilterBuilderConditionSchema` (objectui#9306, same day).
- `element:button` `properties.action`: `@objectstack/spec`'s `InlineActionSchema`, a `z.preprocess(normalizeInlineAction, …)` over an object that is already `.strict()` at its own level.

So the gap was live on the face before this change. The shipped face refuses `{ value: { logic, conditions: [], bogusInGroup } }`, and the unmodified script counted it strict-clean. The corpus just never hit it: today's five `filter-builder` catalog documents have no undeclared key inside `value`, which is why the numbers do not move.

## Gates (at `056efaa9b6`)

- The two tests that name the script, `pnpm exec vitest run --maxWorkers=2 packages/types/src/__tests__/strict-authoring-face-8345.test.ts packages/types/src/__tests__/arm-named-export-8784.test.ts`: `Test Files 2 passed (2)`, `Tests 48 passed (48)`, lock verdict `command-exit 0`.
- `pnpm lint:root`, the root ESLint pass that covers `scripts/`, run in full and not narrowed: 387 files, 0 errors. The changed script has 0 errors and 0 warnings.
- `pnpm check:control-bytes` is OK. `pnpm check:new-line-citations` reports `0 new citation(s)`. `check:entry-guard`, `check:shell-escape-residue`, `check:pre-install-import-graph`, `check:unreferenced-sources` and `check:comment-mask-corpus` all exit 0.
- `node scripts/check-changeset-presence.mjs` reports "No source or published contract of a released package changed in this range, so no changeset is owed." No changeset was added.

## Acceptance notes

Noted here, not filed as cards (no carrier named):

- **Renamed keys in the key probe.** The key probe does not run a preprocessor. So when a preprocessor RENAMES a key, the probe names the old spelling as undeclared on a node both twins accept. Measured in the same scratch root with `element:button` carrying `properties.action.to`: after the change, `properties.action.to` is named while the node is strict-green; before, nothing under that action was named at all. Today's corpora hold no `element:button` document. The docblock says this. The alternative, stopping the probe at an opaque `in`, would instead fail to name every real undeclared key on a preprocessed object.
- **Stale reason in the script's node-boundary paragraph.** The paragraph `THE NODE BOUNDARY, AND WHY IT IS NOT OPTIONAL` gives a reason that stopped being true with objectui#8344: `SchemaNodeSchema`'s component arm is now the component union, not `BaseSchemaCore`. It also names a report field, `documentLevel.strictRefusedWholeTree`, that the report does not have (the real field is `totals.documentsStrictRefusedWholeTree`). Its conclusion still holds: the variant table above measures the boundary as load-bearing, for a different reason (per-node attribution). It is not this card's paragraph, so it is left alone.
- **Stale comment in the shipped walker.** The `case 'pipe'` comment in `packages/types/src/strict-authoring-face.ts` says four pipes are reachable and "today no OBJECT sits on an `out` side, which is why this arm moves no accept set yet". Neither holds on `95a7c8d38f`: see the premise section; the walk finds ten distinct pipe nodes. The walker's behaviour is right, since it refuses every probe above. Only the comment is out of date, and `packages/types/**` is outside this dispatch.
